1 Dated this the 12th day of July, 2024 The application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, by the sole accused in Crime No.640/2024 of the Pandalam Police Station, Pathanamthitta, which is registered against him, for allegedly committing the offences punishable under Sections 366A, 354(A) and 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4(2) r/w Section 3(b) and 8 r/w Section 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The petitioner was arrested and remanded to judicial custody on 02.06.2024.
2.

The prosecution case, in brief, is that; on 31.05.2024, at around 15:00 hrs., the accused kidnapped the victim, aged 15 years, with an intention to commit rape on her and inserted his finger into her genitals.
A case was registered as Crime No.633/2024 under Section 57 of the Kerala Police Act, as the victim was missing.
Consequently, the victim and the accused were BAIL APPL. NO. 5143 OF 2024 apprehended by the railway police at Palakkad and they were taken to the Pandalam Police Station.
During the interrogation of the accused and the victim, the victim said that she was subjected to sexual assault by the accused while travelling in the Himasagar Express Train.

Thus,
the accused has committed the above offences.

3. Heard; Sri.C.A.Anoop, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Smt.Seetha S., the learned Special Public Prosecutor.
4.
The learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently argued that the petitioner is totally innocent of the accusations levelled against him.
In fact, the petitioner and the victim are in love and it was on the victim's own volition that she travelled with the petitioner.
The petitioner has not committed any sexual assault on the victim as alleged by the prosecution.
The petitioner is a 19 year old student and is pursuing his studies.
The petitioner has been in judicial custody for the last 40 days, the investigation in the case is practically complete and BAIL APPL. NO
. 5143 OF 2024 the medical examinations have been conducted.
Therefore, the petitioner's further detention is unnecessary.
Hence, the application may be allowed.
5. The learned Special Public Prosecutor strenuously opposed the application.
The Investigating Officer has filed a bail objection report, inter alia, contending the petitioner has committed sexual assault on the victim.
The medical records clearly prove that the victim has suffered a contusion on the inter part of her genitals.
The accused had kidnapped the victim and was taking her to an unknown destination.
It is only because Crime No.633/2024 was registered, the victim was traced out.
The investigation is in progress.
If the petitioner is released on bail, it would send a very wrong message to the society.
Therefore, the application may be dismissed.
6. The prosecution allegation is that; the petitioner abducted the 15 year old victim and committed penetrative sexual assault on her and outraged her modesty.
Prima facie, the medical records substantiate that the victim has BAIL APPL. NO. 5143 OF 2024 suffered penetrative sexual assault.
Indisputably, the victim is only aged 15 years and was taken away from her lawful guardianship.

Whether the petitioner and the victim were in love is immaterial because the victim is a minor.
7.

In a case of identical circumstances, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in X v. The State of Jharkhand &
Anr [2022 Livelaw SC 194] has categorically held that prima- facie where there are materials to Ashik Sudheesh vs State Of Kerala on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169122484/
2 substantiate that the victim is under the age 18 years, and the accused has committed penetrative sexual assault on her, contention that the parties were in love, has no bearing to the matter.

sentences.text: Uday (supra)
, the appellant and the prosecutrix resided in the same neighbourhood.

As they belonged to different castes,
a matrimonial relationship could not fructify even while physical relations continued between them on the understanding and assurance of marriage.

This Court observed as follows:
"21.

It therefore appears that the consensus of judicial opinion is in favour of the view that the consent given by the prosecutrix to sexual intercourse with a person with whom she is deeply in love on a promise that he would marry her on a later date,
cannot be said to be given under a misconception of fact.
A false promise is not a fact within the meaning of the Code.

We are inclined to agree with this view, but we must add that there is no straitjacket formula for determining whether consent given by the prosecutrix to sexual intercourse is voluntary, or whether it is given under a misconception of fact.

In the ultimate analysis, the tests laid down by the courts provide at best guidance to the judicial mind while considering a question of consent,
but the court must, in each case, consider the evidence before it and the surrounding circumstances, before reaching a conclusion, because each case has its own peculiar facts which may have a bearing on the question whether the consent was voluntary,
or was given under a misconception of fact.
It must also weigh the evidence keeping in view the fact that the burden is on the prosecution to prove each and every ingredient of the offence, absence of consent being one of them."

9. Again in Sujith v. State Of Kerala [2018 (3) KHC 641], this Court after considering Section 20 of the Act has observed as follows :-
"14. S.29 of the Act states that where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under S.3, S.5, S.7 and S.9 of the Act,
the Special Court shall presume, that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, BAIL APPL. NO. 5143 OF 2024 as the case may be,
unless the contrary is proved.

entities.text: Sujith v. State Of Kerala [2018 (3) KHC 641]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the principle that an accused is presumed innocent till found guilty, will not apply to a case under S.3, S.5, S.7 and S.9 of the Act with its full rigor.

The Court shall take into consideration the presumption under S.29 of the Act while dealing with an application for bail filed by a person who is accused of the offences under S.3, S.5, S.7 and S.9 of the Act (See State of Bihar v. Rajballav Prasad, 2016 KHC 6785 : AIR 2017 SC 630 : 2017 (2) SCC 178).

entities.text: State of Bihar v. Rajballav Prasad, 2016 KHC 6785 : AIR 2017 SC 630 : 2017 (2) SCC 178
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
True, a presumption in a criminal case can arise only when the prosecution has adduced the facts forming Ashik Sudheesh vs State Of Kerala on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169122484/
3 the foundation of the case.

sentences.text: In the instant case, prima facie, there are sufficient materials to find the complicity of the petitioner in the crime."

10. In the light of the law referred to in the aforecited decisions and considering the fact that the victim in the case on hand is only 15 years of age, there cannot be any question of consensual sexual relationship between the petitioner and the victim.

11. On an overall consideration of the facts, the rival submissions made across the Bar and the materials placed on record, and on comprehending the nature, seriousness and gravity of the accusations alleged against the petitioner, the prima facie materials that substantiate the petitioner's involvement in the crime, and further that the investigation in the case is in progress and there is every BAIL APPL. NO. 5143 OF 2024 likelihood of the petitioner intimidating the witnesses and tampering with the evidence, I am not satisfied that the petitioner is entitled to be released on bail at this stage.
Resultantly, the application is dismissed.
